_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::pasi#2: the symptom is confirmed and measured, the advice is corrected from a floor to a window. Upstream pasi_twoway_disprelaxaitken_particle_dem_1d_normalcontact_linspring_walldiscretcond.4C.yaml drops one DEM particle of diameter 1.0 onto a clamped 1.75x1.75 membrane; the membrane is regenerated as an NxN QUAD4 patch over the same square so h_structure is the only thing that varies, with identical instrumentation in every arm. At h/d = 0.583 the interface has 4 free nodes, every moving node deflects by exactly the same amount (peak/mean = 1.000) — the entry's 'stress field looks uniform', literally — while at h/d = 0.250 there are 36 free nodes, a real contact patch with peak/mean 5.063, and the regenerated deck reproduces the shipped answer with all six particle result tests correct. But refining past that is fatal: at h/d = 0.146 the partitioned loop dies with 'The partitioned PASI solver did not converge in ITEMAX steps!' from pasi/4C_pasi_partitioned_twowaycoup.cpp line 419 — the identical sentence produced by the too-coarse h/d = 0.875 arm. One diagnostic, two opposite causes, and it names neither the mesh nor the particle diameter nor the interface. So the entry's target of h ~ 0.5*d sits inside the admissible band but must not be read as a floor. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: The partitioned PASI solver did not converge in ITEMAX steps!

_mutation.note: remove the over-refined arm: point it at the admissible N = 7 mesh instead of the N = 12 one. The divergence disappears, DIVERGED_N12 becomes 0 and EXIT_N12 becomes 0, so the evidence that refining past the entry's target is fatal is gone and the fixture must go red.

remove the coarse-interface arm: build it at N = 7 as well. Its interface then carries 36 moving nodes with a peak/mean of 5.063 instead of 4 nodes at exactly 1.000, so MOVING_INTERFACE_NODES_N3, DEFLECTION_PEAK_OVER_MEAN_N3 and COARSE_INTERFACE_RESPONSE_IS_UNIFORM all change and the fixture must go red.
